target.title: feat: add session thread management
target.body: Related: #54397 Closes #88568 AI-assisted: yes. Implementation and redesign were reviewed with the repository's structured autoreview workflow. ## What Problem This Solves OpenClaw sessions are durable conversation threads, but their management controls were fragmented: frequent sessions disappear into recency ordering, stale sessions stay in every active list unless deleted, and renaming was disconnected from the Chat surfaces. The first iteration of this PR added the controls but rendered three always-visible bordered buttons on every picker row, which crushed session labels and made the picker read as a toolbar instead of a list. ## Why This Change Was Made Pin, archive/restore, and rename land on the existing session model instead of a second topic store: `sessions.list` separates active and archived sessions, `sessions.patch` owns management mutations, and live `sessions.changed` events keep every subscribed UI coherent. Archived chat sessions become read-only, lifecycle fencing keeps concurrent runs/compaction from resurrecting archived state, and the SDK plus Swift protocol expose the same contracts. The management UI is redesigned to be minimal, following the pattern of modern thread lists (e.g. the Codex app): - Rows are single text lines: label left, relative timestamp right. - Rename/archive/pin actions stay invisible until the row is hovered or focused (`:focus-within` keeps them keyboard-reachable); the pin action doubles as the accent pinned badge, so it stays visible for pinned rows. - Sessions with an active run show a spinner in the trailing slot instead of the timestamp — a working indicator visible in both the sidebar recents and the chat picker. - The sidebar recents float pinned sessions above recency (shared comparator with the picker and Sessions view) and gain the same archive/pin actions through the unified archive fallback, so archiving the current session from any surface switches Chat back to the agent main session. - One shared archive policy (`canArchiveSessionRow`) protects agent main sessions, live runs, and global/unknown scopes across the sidebar, picker, and Sessions table. - Full session detail (surface, model, absolute timestamp) moved into the row tooltip; on touch devices, the picker keeps actions visible since there is no hover. ## User Impact Users can now: - rename, pin/unpin, and archive sessions directly from the Chat session picker and the sidebar recents list; - see pinned sessions above newer unpinned sessions in every session list, marked by an accent pin badge; - see at a glance which sessions are actively running (spinner working indicator); - switch the Sessions page into an archived-only view and restore sessions without losing transcripts; - inspect archived sessions through `sessions_list`. Agent main sessions and sessions with active runs cannot be archived. Archiving clears the pin, archived chat sessions are read-only, and archiving the selected session from any surface returns the UI to that agent's main session. ### Before / After Chat session picker — before (always-visible bordered buttons, truncated labels) vs after (minimal rows, hover-revealed actions, pinned badge, run spinner): Sidebar recents — pinned badge on Release planning, run spinner on Data migration, hover-revealed archive/pin on Research notes: ## Evidence - `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/ui/e2e/session-management.e2e.test.ts` — real Chromium GUI flow covering pinned-first sidebar ordering, run spinner in both surfaces, hover/focus reveal (computed-opacity assertions), pinned badge without hover, main-session archive protection, and rename/pin/archive patch round-trips. Screenshots above are captured by this run. - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/ui/views/chat.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts ui/src/ui/app-chat.test.ts` — 440 tests passed. - Gateway/session lifecycle suites: `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts`. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` — passed. - `pnpm build` — passed, including the Control UI production bundle; no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings. - Structured autoreview — clean after addressing findings (see PR comments for the review trail). - Fixed in redesign: the active-run tooltip used a non-existent locale key (`sessions.sessionDetails.activeRun`); both surfaces now use `sessionsView.activeRun`. - Integration with mailbox-era `main`: gateway agent admission now treats a session as deleted only when both the requested and canonical alias sets miss it — a canonical-only re-read misreported legacy bare-`main` stores as deleted, while a requested-only read broke exec-approval followups (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts`); `sessions_list` mailbox test expectations learned the `archived`/`pinned` row fields; cron persist tests keep one consistent store across claim-guarded persist calls; dead lifecycle writes flagged by `no-useless-assignment` removed.

target.title: fix(auth-profiles): scope subscription_limit blocks to the failing model
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #99809. When OpenAI's Codex WHAM usage probe returns a `subscription_limit` block for one model (e.g. `gpt-5.5`), OpenClaw currently blocks the entire shared auth profile — including other models on that same profile with a genuinely separate quota pool (e.g. a Codex "spark" variant). The `blockedModel` field already existed in the type system for exactly this scoping, but the WHAM write path (`applyWhamCooldownResult`) discarded it (`blockedModel: void 0`), and the gating read paths (`resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, `shouldBypassModelScopedCooldown`, `isProfileInCooldown`, `getSoonestCooldownExpiry`) never consulted it — unlike the existing `cooldownModel` scoping used for `rate_limit`/`timeout`.

## Changes

- `applyWhamCooldownResult` now threads `modelId` into `blockedModel` instead of discarding it.
- `resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, `shouldBypassModelScopedCooldown`, `isProfileInCooldown`, and `getSoonestCooldownExpiry` now respect `blockedModel` scoping, mirroring the existing `cooldownModel` scoping already used for `rate_limit`/`timeout`.
- Added `mergeBlockedModel`: when a new `subscription_limit` block lands while an existing `blockedUntil` is still active on the same profile, it only narrows `blockedModel` to the incoming model if the existing block already agreed with it (same model, or no existing active block). Otherwise — existing block is unscoped, or scoped to a *different* model than the incoming one — it widens to profile-wide (`undefined`) so neither model's coverage is silently dropped.

## Evidence

Real `vitest` run against this branch (not a hand-mirrored script), scoped to the affected file:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts

 ✓ |agents-core| ... scopes a subscription_limit block to the failing model so other models on the same profile stay usable
 ✓ |agents-core| ... widens to profile-wide when a new model-scoped block lands on top of an already-active unscoped block
 ✓ |agents-core| ... widens to profile-wide when a new block for a different model conflicts with an existing model-scoped block
 ✓ |agents-core| ... keeps a repeated block for the same model scoped to just that model

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
   Duration  7.04s
```

Covers the three review asks directly:
- **Real runtime proof** — output above is a live `vitest` run against the actual patched `usage.ts`, not a mirrored script.
- **Existing `blockedUntil` + `blockedModel` combo** — new tests seed a store with an already-active `blockedUntil` (both unscoped and model-scoped) and assert on the resulting `blockedModel` after a second block lands.
- **Old unscoped/conflicting-model blocks stay profile-wide** — the two "widens to profile-wide" tests assert `blockedModel` is `undefined` after merging with a pre-existing unscoped block or a conflicting model-scoped block, and that `isProfileInCooldown` still returns `true` for every previously-covered model plus the profile-wide check.

target.title: fix(config): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in unsetConfigValueAtPath
target.body:
## Summary
Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of the `in` operator in `unsetConfigValueAtPath()` to prevent prototype chain pollution when checking whether a config key exists before deletion.

## What Problem This Solves
When calling `unsetConfigValueAtPath(root, ["foo", "toString"])` on a config object that does **not** have a `toString` key, the function returns `true` (claiming success) because `"toString" in cursor` matches `Object.prototype.toString`.

**The function lies to its caller** — it reports "key found and deleted" when the key never existed. This can cause config management tools (CLI `config unset`, config merge logic) to silently skip error handling for non-existent keys.

**Code evidence**: In `src/config/config-paths.ts:63`, `if (!(leafKey in cursor))` checks the prototype chain. `cursor` is a plain `PathNode` object (`Record<string, unknown>`), and `leafKey` comes from user-provided dot-notation paths like `foo.toString`.

## Root Cause
- The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, not just own properties
- `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022+) correctly checks only the object's own properties
- `Object.hasOwn` is already used 15+ times across the codebase — this was a missed instance

## Why This Fix
- **Minimal**: 1-line change, same pattern as #99129
- **Consistent**: matches existing `Object.hasOwn` usage in the codebase
- **Regression-safe**: normal keys pass unchanged; only prototype keys are affected

## Evidence
- **Before**: `unsetConfigValueAtPath({foo:{bar:"v"}}, ["foo","toString"])` returns `true` (wrong — key doesn't exist)
- **After**: returns `false` (correct — key is not an own property)
- All 3 prototype keys tested: toString, constructor, valueOf — all correctly return false
- Existing non-prototype key deletion: unaffected
- Parent pruning: unaffected

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
FAIL non-existent "toString" returns false (got: true, owns "toString": false)
FAIL non-existent "constructor" returns false (got: true, owns "constructor": false)
FAIL non-existent "valueOf" returns false (got: true, owns "valueOf": false)
FAIL non-existent "hasOwnProperty" returns false (got: true, owns "hasOwnProperty": false)
PASS existing "toString" deleted successfully
PASS "toString" no longer own property
PASS sibling key "bar" preserved
PASS parent "foo" preserved after no-op unset
PASS sibling "bar" preserved after no-op unset

4 FAILED
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
PASS non-existent "toString" returns false (got: false, owns "toString": false)
PASS non-existent "constructor" returns false (got: false, owns "constructor": false)
PASS non-existent "valueOf" returns false (got: false, owns "valueOf": false)
PASS non-existent "hasOwnProperty" returns false (got: false, owns "hasOwnProperty": false)
PASS existing "toString" deleted successfully
PASS "toString" no longer own property
PASS sibling key "bar" preserved
PASS parent "foo" preserved after no-op unset
PASS sibling "bar" preserved after no-op unset

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- Regression test added: `src/config/config-paths.test.ts` covers 3 prototype keys + normal deletion + parent pruning
- Fix verified with standalone `node --import tsx` proof script
- Diff: 1 line changed in source + regression test
- Proof: 4 prototype keys (toString/constructor/valueOf/hasOwnProperty) all change from FAIL → PASS, regression tests pass

target.title: fix(ui): keep composer on Send when run-status toast expires (#88033)
target.body:
## Summary

The webchat composer button could snap back to the red **Stop** button several seconds *after* a response had visibly completed (issue #88033, step 5: "it returns to the send button and then many seconds later, it returns to the Stop button even though it didn't start thinking again").

### Root cause

When a local turn finishes, `reconcileChatRunLifecycle` publishes a ~5s run-status toast and arms an in-window stale-row reconcile. While the toast is showing, `hasTerminalRunStatus` masks any stale "active" selected-session row. If a racing `sessions.list` refresh re-introduces that stale active row (the backend run is already done; the row is only kept "active" by poll lag), the masking ends the instant the toast clears — so the composer reverts to **Stop** with no real active run.

### Fix

In `scheduleRunStatusClear`, when the toast timer fires, re-run the in-window stale-row reconcile (`reconcileChatRunFromCurrentSessionRow(host, { publishRunStatus: false })`). `publishRunStatus:false` ensures this does not re-arm another toast and loop. The composer now stays on **Send** once the run is terminal.

This path (`run-lifecycle.ts` toast expiry) was not touched by the two earlier closed attempts (#88041, #88045).

### Scope
- `ui/src/ui/chat/run-lifecycle.ts` — 1 line + explanatory comment in `scheduleRunStatusClear`
- `ui/src/ui/chat/run-lifecycle.test.ts` — deterministic regression test (fake timers)

Net: +45 / −1 across 2 files.

## Verification / Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Webchat composer reverting from Send back to the red Stop button seconds after a completed run, when a stale `sessions.list` active row is unmasked on run-status toast expiry.
- **Real environment tested:** Local source checkout, Node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.2.2, Vitest unit-ui project (`test/vitest/vitest.unit-ui.config.ts`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test ui/src/ui/chat/run-lifecycle.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix:** `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13)`. Red/green proof: with the one-line reconcile removed the new test fails at `expect(rowActive(host)).toBe(false)` (`expected true to be false`); with the fix restored all 13 pass. `oxfmt --check` and oxlint on both files are clean.
- **Observed result after fix:** When the run-status toast expires, the stale active session row is reconciled to terminal, so the composer stays on **Send** instead of snapping back to **Stop**.
- **What was not tested:** No live browser/Gateway end-to-end run (the original report is an intermittent timing race driven by poll lag); covered here by a deterministic fake-timer unit test that reproduces the exact race.

Fixes #88033

target.title: fix: video media understanding runs without a selected model

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on automatic video media understanding could select a video-capable provider without a model and then execute video description with `model` unset.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was that video provider entry resolution did not apply the same invariant as model-backed media execution: a provider selected for video could be returned without a model, and that unset value was passed into `describeVideo`. Video auto-selection now resolves the provider default video model for active and key-selected providers; providers without a resolvable video model are skipped instead of being run with an undefined model. ## User Impact

Video attachments can be described through auto-selected providers such as Moonshot without silently dropping the model id. target.title: feat(codex): share native threads across Codex clients
target.body:
Closes #99781

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's Codex harness isolates each agent in a private Codex home, so threads created in Codex Desktop or the CLI are invisible to OpenClaw, and OpenClaw-created threads are invisible to native Codex clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `appServer.homeScope: "user"` mode that connects the stdio app-server to the native user Codex home and authentication. An owner-only `codex_threads` tool lists, reads, forks, renames, archives, and restores native threads; continuation is fork-first so two clients never write the same thread concurrently.

The existing per-agent isolated home remains the default. Shared-user-home mode is intentionally rejected for remote WebSocket transports.

## User Impact

Operators can opt a Codex-backed OpenClaw agent into the same thread store used by Codex Desktop and the CLI, inspect and manage those native threads from OpenClaw, and attach a safe native fork to the current OpenClaw session.

## Evidence

- Live cross-process proof: three independent bundled Codex app-server processes create/list/read/fork/rename/archive/unarchive through one shared native home (`OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_THREAD_COEXISTENCE=1 node scripts/test-live.mjs -- extensions/codex/src/native-thread-coexistence.live.test.ts`).

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites (post-rebase onto `upstream/main`): WhatsApp **986/986**, Discord **1832/1832**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).
- SDK contract: `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` (`accept`/`pending`/`complete`/`release`, now `fail`) was already public API through `channel-outbound` — WhatsApp's inbound monitor consumes it from that exact barrel pre-dating this PR. This PR documents the full facade (`docs/plugins/sdk-channel-outbound.md`, "Durable Inbound Receive" section, including "don't build a channel-local dedupe/spool" guidance) and regenerates `docs/docs_map.md`. This is also the intended next step for other channels: Telegram's `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-spool.ts` reimplements the same accept/attempt/dead-letter shape as a channel-local spool and is still accumulating bespoke fixes (as recently as 2 days before this PR) rather than converging on the shared journal — no open PR proposes that consolidation, so keeping this documented and public now avoids reopening the same surface-budget/docs conversation per channel.

**Real gateway restart-replay proof (LINE)** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`).

Discord and Mattermost flip the exact same shared SDK mechanism (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`) that LINE's live proof exercises — only the channel-specific admission/webhook wrapper differs. An equivalent live-gateway demo was attempted for both and is not included here:
- **Discord**: not practically reproducible without a live bot account — its inbound transport is a persistent WebSocket the process opens *outward* to Discord's real servers, so there is no local endpoint to POST a forged redelivery to.
- **Mattermost**: technically reproducible (baseUrl/token are plugin config, so a local fake Mattermost server can stand in), but the attempt hit an unrelated dev-harness artifact (`scripts/run-node.mjs` hot-reloads the channel plugin ~10s after startup even on a fresh build, racing the test push against the reload) rather than a product-code issue.

Both channels have their own real, SQLite-backed regression tests exercising the identical persistent guard through the actual channel handler (not a mock): `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` (drives the real `createDiscordMessageHandler`), and `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`.

**Real cross-process proof of the WhatsApp bounded-replay fix.** WhatsApp's durable-inbound replay trigger is local (it fires on socket attach against on-disk pending state, not on a live platform round-trip), so this mechanism was exercised directly with the actual shipped code from this branch — `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts` and the exact `WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` constant from `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/durable-receive.ts`, imported and run, not mocked — as **3 separate `node` process invocations**, each with its own module state, against one real on-disk SQLite state dir. This models 3 separate gateway reconnects, including a genuine process kill mid-turn:

Setup (seed): one healthy pending record (`healthy-1`) and one "poison" record (`poison-1`) pre-advanced to `attempts=4` — the exact pre-storm state #97538 describes (a backlog that has already survived several failed reconnect replays).

*Reconnect 1* (new process): `healthy-1` processes and completes normally. `poison-1`'s handler is made to hang forever (models #97538 Bug 1's wedged `embedded_run` lane) — the process is killed via a 3s timeout instead of waiting forever, the same way a real gateway restart would end a wedged run:
```
[phase 1] force-exiting after 3s (simulated crash while poison-1 was wedged)
```
SQLite after the kill: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|pending|5`. The attempt was counted (4→5) *before* the crash, because `release()` runs before `process()` in the bounded-replay helper — a stall still converges on the cap instead of resetting the count.

*Reconnect 2* (new process): `poison-1` is now at the cap and is dead-lettered without ever calling its handler again — no further storm:
```
[phase 2] dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts: id=poison-1 attempts=5
[phase 2] pending after replay: []
```

*Reconnect 3* (new process): stays dead — pending is empty, and a simulated platform redelivery of the same id (WhatsApp commonly resends via multi-device/offline sync) is recognized as already-terminal and not reprocessed:
```
[phase 3] redelivery of dead-lettered poison-1 => kind=pending duplicate=true
```
Final state: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|failed|5` — the healthy message delivered normally throughout, the poison message stopped storming after exactly 5 total attempts and never came back.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).

target.title: fix(qqbot): strip echoed inbound metadata from replies
target.body:
﻿Closes #97980

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users could see OpenClaw's internal inbound metadata at the start of replies, such as `Conversation info (untrusted metadata)` and `Sender (untrusted metadata)` JSON blocks, before the actual assistant response.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQ Bot now runs outbound-visible text through a plugin-owned sanitizer that keeps the existing assistant-visible text cleanup and strips leading echoed inbound metadata blocks before delivery. The same sanitizer is used by the QQ outbound adapter surface, by the direct QQ gateway dispatch path, and by the official C2C streaming path.

The direct QQ gateway path sanitizes block reply text before silent-reply classification as well as before delivery. That keeps metadata-prefixed `NO_REPLY` and `[SKIP]` control replies suppressed instead of stripping the metadata after the silence check and accidentally sending the control token.

The official C2C streaming path still keeps raw text for reply-boundary detection, but sanitizes the normalized visible text before starting or updating a QQ stream. Metadata-only partial updates are held until real visible answer text arrives, so the metadata block is not streamed first.

The change stays local to the QQ Bot plugin and does not alter the prompt envelope sent to the model.

## User Impact

QQ Bot replies no longer expose technical OpenClaw context blocks to end users when a model echoes the inbound prompt metadata. Users see only the intended assistant response text across adapter sends, direct static dispatch, and official C2C streaming, and metadata-prefixed silent replies remain silent.

target.title: fix(auth-profiles): scope subscription_limit blocks to the failing model
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #99809. When OpenAI's Codex WHAM usage probe returns a `subscription_limit` block for one model (e.g. `gpt-5.5`), OpenClaw currently blocks the entire shared auth profile — including other models on that same profile with a genuinely separate quota pool (e.g. a Codex "spark" variant). The `blockedModel` field already existed in the type system for exactly this scoping, but the WHAM write path (`applyWhamCooldownResult`) discarded it (`blockedModel: void 0`), and the gating read paths (`resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, `shouldBypassModelScopedCooldown`, `isProfileInCooldown`, `getSoonestCooldownExpiry`) never consulted it — unlike the existing `cooldownModel` scoping used for `rate_limit`/`timeout`.

## Changes

- `applyWhamCooldownResult` now threads `modelId` into `blockedModel` instead of discarding it.
- `resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, `shouldBypassModelScopedCooldown`, `isProfileInCooldown`, and `getSoonestCooldownExpiry` now respect `blockedModel` scoping, mirroring the existing `cooldownModel` scoping already used for `rate_limit`/`timeout`.
- Added `mergeBlockedModel`: when a new `subscription_limit` block lands while an existing `blockedUntil` is still active on the same profile, it only narrows `blockedModel` to the incoming model if the existing block already agreed with it (same model, or no existing active block). Otherwise — existing block is unscoped, or scoped to a *different* model than the incoming one — it widens to profile-wide (`undefined`) so neither model's coverage is silently dropped.

## Evidence

Real `vitest` run against this branch (not a hand-mirrored script), scoped to the affected file:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts

 ✓ |agents-core| ... scopes a subscription_limit block to the failing model so other models on the same profile stay usable
 ✓ |agents-core| ... widens to profile-wide when a new model-scoped block lands on top of an already-active unscoped block
 ✓ |agents-core| ... widens to profile-wide when a new block for a different model conflicts with an existing model-scoped block
 ✓ |agents-core| ... keeps a repeated block for the same model scoped to just that model

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
   Duration  7.04s
```

Covers the three review asks directly:
- **Real runtime proof** — output above is a live `vitest` run against the actual patched `usage.ts`, not a mirrored script.
- **Existing `blockedUntil` + `blockedModel` combo** — new tests seed a store with an already-active `blockedUntil` (both unscoped and model-scoped) and assert on the resulting `blockedModel` after a second block lands.
- **Old unscoped/conflicting-model blocks stay profile-wide** — the two "widens to profile-wide" tests assert `blockedModel` is `undefined` after merging with a pre-existing unscoped block or a conflicting model-scoped block, and that `isProfileInCooldown` still returns `true` for every previously-covered model plus the profile-wide check.

target.title: fix(feishu): upgrade single newlines to paragraph breaks in post md messages
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When OpenClaw sends messages to Feishu via `msg_type: post` with `tag: md`, single newline characters (`\n`) are rendered as plain spaces by the Feishu IM API. This causes multi-paragraph prose to appear visually cramped. Fixes #97074 ## Why This Change Was Made Added `normalizeFeishuPostMarkdownNewlines()` — a dedicated function that upgrades single `\n` to `\n\n` outside code regions for Feishu post+md rendering. It runs only after the render mode is known, so card and document-comment text are never modified. **Revision 6** (per ClawSweeper re-review — table conversion ordering): 1. **[P2] Convert tables before normalization in outbound post path** — `sendOutboundText` now resolves the table mode and runs `convertMarkdownTables` before `normalizeFeishuPostMarkdownNewlines`. Normalization was inserting blank lines between table rows, which broke table row contiguity for the converter. Converting first preserves table structure for raw-mode Feishu accounts. `sendMessageFeishu` runs `convertMarkdownTables` again internally, but that is a no-op on already-converted text. This prevents the second normalization pass from expanding code-block newlines when a chunk boundary falls inside a fenced region. 3. **[P2] Reply fanout for expanded subchunks** — Only the first subchunk carries the reply target. target.title: fix(config): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in unsetConfigValueAtPath
target.body:
## Summary
Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of the `in` operator in `unsetConfigValueAtPath()` to prevent prototype chain pollution when checking whether a config key exists before deletion.

## What Problem This Solves
When calling `unsetConfigValueAtPath(root, ["foo", "toString"])` on a config object that does **not** have a `toString` key, the function returns `true` (claiming success) because `"toString" in cursor` matches `Object.prototype.toString`.

**The function lies to its caller** — it reports "key found and deleted" when the key never existed. This can cause config management tools (CLI `config unset`, config merge logic) to silently skip error handling for non-existent keys.

**Code evidence**: In `src/config/config-paths.ts:63`, `if (!(leafKey in cursor))` checks the prototype chain. `cursor` is a plain `PathNode` object (`Record<string, unknown>`), and `leafKey` comes from user-provided dot-notation paths like `foo.toString`.

## Root Cause
- The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, not just own properties
- `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022+) correctly checks only the object's own properties
- `Object.hasOwn` is already used 15+ times across the codebase — this was a missed instance

## Why This Fix
- **Minimal**: 1-line change, same pattern as #99129
- **Consistent**: matches existing `Object.hasOwn` usage in the codebase
- **Regression-safe**: normal keys pass unchanged; only prototype keys are affected

## Evidence
- **Before**: `unsetConfigValueAtPath({foo:{bar:"v"}}, ["foo","toString"])` returns `true` (wrong — key doesn't exist)
- **After**: returns `false` (correct — key is not an own property)
- All 3 prototype keys tested: toString, constructor, valueOf — all correctly return false
- Existing non-prototype key deletion: unaffected
- Parent pruning: unaffected

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
FAIL non-existent "toString" returns false (got: true, owns "toString": false)
FAIL non-existent "constructor" returns false (got: true, owns "constructor": false)
FAIL non-existent "valueOf" returns false (got: true, owns "valueOf": false)
FAIL non-existent "hasOwnProperty" returns false (got: true, owns "hasOwnProperty": false)
PASS existing "toString" deleted successfully
PASS "toString" no longer own property
PASS sibling key "bar" preserved
PASS parent "foo" preserved after no-op unset
PASS sibling "bar" preserved after no-op unset

4 FAILED
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
PASS non-existent "toString" returns false (got: false, owns "toString": false)
PASS non-existent "constructor" returns false (got: false, owns "constructor": false)
PASS non-existent "valueOf" returns false (got: false, owns "valueOf": false)
PASS non-existent "hasOwnProperty" returns false (got: false, owns "hasOwnProperty": false)
PASS existing "toString" deleted successfully
PASS "toString" no longer own property
PASS sibling key "bar" preserved
PASS parent "foo" preserved after no-op unset
PASS sibling "bar" preserved after no-op unset

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- Regression test added: `src/config/config-paths.test.ts` covers 3 prototype keys + normal deletion + parent pruning
- Fix verified with standalone `node --import tsx` proof script
- Diff: 1 line changed in source + regression test
- Proof: 4 prototype keys (toString/constructor/valueOf/hasOwnProperty) all change from FAIL → PASS, regression tests pass

target.title: fix(ui): keep composer on Send when run-status toast expires (#88033)
target.body:
## Summary

The webchat composer button could snap back to the red **Stop** button several seconds *after* a response had visibly completed (issue #88033, step 5: "it returns to the send button and then many seconds later, it returns to the Stop button even though it didn't start thinking again").

### Root cause

When a local turn finishes, `reconcileChatRunLifecycle` publishes a ~5s run-status toast and arms an in-window stale-row reconcile. While the toast is showing, `hasTerminalRunStatus` masks any stale "active" selected-session row. If a racing `sessions.list` refresh re-introduces that stale active row (the backend run is already done; the row is only kept "active" by poll lag), the masking ends the instant the toast clears — so the composer reverts to **Stop** with no real active run.

### Fix

In `scheduleRunStatusClear`, when the toast timer fires, re-run the in-window stale-row reconcile (`reconcileChatRunFromCurrentSessionRow(host, { publishRunStatus: false })`). `publishRunStatus:false` ensures this does not re-arm another toast and loop. The composer now stays on **Send** once the run is terminal.

This path (`run-lifecycle.ts` toast expiry) was not touched by the two earlier closed attempts (#88041, #88045).

### Scope
- `ui/src/ui/chat/run-lifecycle.ts` — 1 line + explanatory comment in `scheduleRunStatusClear`
- `ui/src/ui/chat/run-lifecycle.test.ts` — deterministic regression test (fake timers)

Net: +45 / −1 across 2 files.

## Verification / Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Webchat composer reverting from Send back to the red Stop button seconds after a completed run, when a stale `sessions.list` active row is unmasked on run-status toast expiry.
- **Real environment tested:** Local source checkout, Node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.2.2, Vitest unit-ui project (`test/vitest/vitest.unit-ui.config.ts`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test ui/src/ui/chat/run-lifecycle.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix:** `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13)`. Red/green proof: with the one-line reconcile removed the new test fails at `expect(rowActive(host)).toBe(false)` (`expected true to be false`); with the fix restored all 13 pass. `oxfmt --check` and oxlint on both files are clean.
- **Observed result after fix:** When the run-status toast expires, the stale active session row is reconciled to terminal, so the composer stays on **Send** instead of snapping back to **Stop**.
- **What was not tested:** No live browser/Gateway end-to-end run (the original report is an intermittent timing race driven by poll lag); covered here by a deterministic fake-timer unit test that reproduces the exact race.

Fixes #88033

target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
﻿﻿﻿﻿Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into both gateway-host and node-host approval analysis. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

The follow-up update also covers foreground gateway runtime forms that were missed by the first patch: `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway --force`, and option-only gateway run surfaces such as `--port`. Read-only gateway inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway call ...`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior and read-only status/query commands are unchanged.

## Evidence

Issue review feedback incorporated: lifecycle classification now has regression coverage for the ordering invariant that classification happens before durable allowlist trust or auto-review decisions.

Latest review feedback incorporated at `d6c702f501c6`: systemctl action discovery now skips value-taking options before the lifecycle verb, so `systemctl -s TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service` and `systemctl --signal=TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service` are classified before allowlist or auto-review can run. A read-only regression keeps `systemctl --type service status openclaw-gateway.service` outside the lifecycle guard.

Latest review feedback incorporated at `a7ef45f423aa`: `openclaw gateway call` is now method-aware instead of being treated as a read-only subcommand family. Lifecycle-affecting RPC calls such as `update.run` and `gateway.restart.request` require explicit lifecycle approval before durable allowlist or auto-review can run, while read-only RPCs such as `health`, `update.status`, and `logs.tail` remain outside the lifecycle guard.

Live gateway-host proof from an isolated branch gateway (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <random> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, independent temp state/config):

```json
{
  "branchHead": "0ce214f5c1a1",
  "isolatedGateway": {
    "healthOk": true
  },
  "lifecycleAllowlistOnMissAutoReview": {
    "command": "openclaw gateway --force",
    "autoReviewCalls": 0,
    "resultStatus": "approval-unavailable",
    "hasLifecycleWarning": true,
    "warningCount": 1
  },
  "yoloFullOff": {
    "command": "openclaw gateway --force",
    "allowedWithoutPending": true,
    "warningCount": 0
  }
}
```

`approval-unavailable` is expected in this isolated proof because no approval delivery route is configured; it is still a blocking approval result before command execution, and `autoReviewCalls: 0` proves the lifecycle command was not laundered through auto-review first. The `yoloFullOff` case confirms `security=full` + `ask=off` remains unchanged.

```shell

# Tests  144 passed | 111 skipped (255)
```

target.title: fix(ssh-tunnel): handle spawn error to prevent unhandled rejection crash
target.body:
## Summary

Add a child-process `error` listener in `startSshPortForward` so missing `/usr/bin/ssh` (ENOENT) rejects the tunnel Promise instead of emitting an unhandled error that crashes the process.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: `spawn("/usr/bin/ssh", ...)` emits async `error` event. Without a listener, Node.js throws an unhandled `error` event and crashes the process. The existing `child.once("exit", ...)` never fires on spawn failure, so the `Promise.race` hangs until timeout.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw main

**Exact steps run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The new test "rejects with the spawn error when ssh binary is missing" constructs a mock child that emits `error` via `queueMicrotask`, matching real asynchronous spawn behavior, and verifies the tunnel start Promise rejects with "ENOENT".

**Before-fix evidence**: `child.once("exit", ...)` was the only listener. A spawn ENOENT would emit `error` asynchronously, the `exit` listener would never fire, and the unhandled `error` event would crash the process.

**Observed result after fix**: `child.once("error", reject)` forwards spawn failures into the Promise rejection path. The `Promise.race` rejects with the ENOENT error instead of hanging.

**What was not tested**: Live system without `/usr/bin/ssh` (not possible in CI). The test verifies the exact Node.js spawn error contract.

## Risk

Low. One-line addition in an existing Promise constructor. Does not change the happy path.

## Summary

`ResolvedConversationCapabilityProfile.conversation.scope` now classifies the conversation audience exclusively from server-verified or trust-checked inputs, in this precedence:

1. Live chat type: `direct` -> `direct`; `group`/`channel` -> `shared`.
2. Server-derived session keys: when `runSessionKey` or `sessionKey` names a group/channel conversation (new `sessionKeyNamesGroupConversation` helper in `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts`), scope is `shared` even without a live chat type. This also covers runs whose policy key is a sandbox alias while the live run session is a group.
3. Trust-checked group facts: caller group facts count only when `resolveTrustedGroupId` vouched for them. When the trust check dropped the caller group id, scope resolves `unknown` instead of `shared`.

Previously the fallback branch (no usable chat type) read the raw caller-supplied `groupId`/`groupChannel`/`groupSpace` params, while the same profile published those fields trust-checked (`null` when dropped). An unvouched caller-controlled group value could therefore classify an unknown-audience conversation as `shared` in the exact field that conversation identity modes (#98542) and scoped brokered credentials (#98549 / #98707) are specified to consume for audience and credential decisions. The profile also now computes the masked `groupChannel`/`groupSpace` once and reuses them for group-policy resolution, the published conversation fields, and scope, so the three can no longer diverge.

`conversation.scope` has zero consumers on current main (verified by grep across `src/`, `extensions/`, `packages/`), so the semantics change is contract-safe now and becomes the guaranteed baseline before the first consumers land.

## Proof (local)

- `pnpm tsgo` clean.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.test.ts` — 6 passed, including new regressions:
  - dropped caller group facts -> `scope: "unknown"`, published group fields `null`;
  - group-scoped session key without live chat type -> `shared`;
  - live run session key behind a sandbox policy key -> `shared`;
  - session-vouched caller group -> `shared`, `dropped: false`.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

## Non-goals

- No change to group tool-policy resolution or `resolveTrustedGroupId` semantics; only scope classification and shared computation of the already-masked fields.
- No new config or public API surface. `sessionKeyNamesGroupConversation` is an internal helper.

target.title: fix(markdown-core): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in parseFrontmatterBlock
target.body:
## Summary
Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of the `in` operator in `parseFrontmatterBlock()` to prevent prototype chain pollution when merging line-parsed frontmatter entries.

## What Problem This Solves
When YAML frontmatter contains a key named after an `Object.prototype` property (e.g., `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`) with a `null` value, the key is **silently dropped** from the output.

**Root cause**: `coerceYamlFrontmatterValue(null)` returns `undefined`, causing the YAML parser to skip the key. The inline line parser still captures it, but the merge step at `frontmatter.ts:225` uses `key in merged` — which traverses the prototype chain. Since `"toString" in {}` is `true` (it finds `Object.prototype.toString`), the inline value is also discarded, and the user's data is lost.

**Code evidence**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts:225`, the code checks `if (!(key in merged))` — but `merged = {}` inherits from `Object.prototype`, so prototype keys are falsely detected as "already present".

## Root Cause
- The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, not just own properties
- `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022+) correctly checks only the object's own properties
- `Object.hasOwn` is already used 15+ times across the codebase (`src/infra/`, `src/param-key.ts`, `packages/agent-core/`, etc.) — this was the one remaining `in` operator usage on a plain object

## Why This Fix
- **Minimal**: 1-line change, no behavioral impact on normal keys
- **Consistent**: matches existing `Object.hasOwn` usage pattern in the codebase
- **Correct**: `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` is the semantically correct check for "does this object own this property"
- **Regression-safe**: normal keys pass unchanged; only prototype keys are affected

## Evidence
- **Before**: `toString: null` in YAML frontmatter → output `{title: "Hello"}` (toString **lost**)
- **After**: `toString: null` in YAML frontmatter → output `{title: "Hello", toString: "null"}` (toString **preserved**)
- All 4 prototype keys tested: toString, constructor, valueOf, hasOwnProperty — all preserved
- Normal keys regression check: passed

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-frontmatter.mjs
FAIL: 'toString' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'toString' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
FAIL: 'constructor' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'constructor' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
FAIL: 'valueOf' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'valueOf' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
FAIL: 'hasOwnProperty' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'hasOwnProperty' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
PASS: normal key 'title' preserved (got: "Hello")

8 FAILED
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-frontmatter.mjs
PASS: 'toString' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'toString' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: 'constructor' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'constructor' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: 'valueOf' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'valueOf' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: 'hasOwnProperty' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'hasOwnProperty' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: normal key 'title' preserved (got: "Hello")

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check`: passed (only pre-existing `npm shrinkwrap guard` failure, unrelated)
- Manual verification: 4 prototype keys + normal keys regression tested
- Diff: 1 line changed, 1 file

target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fix classification: Root-cause feature completion for opt-in model-created session titles.
- Root cause: Saved sessions had no durable generated-title source of truth, so session lists fell back to manual names, first user message snippets, or session ids.
- Why this is root-cause fix: `autoTitle` is created once in the reply lifecycle, stored on the session entry, preserved without refreshing session activity, cleared with reset/rollover state, and projected to gateway/Control UI instead of being recomputed by display fallbacks.
- Patch quality notes: The broad catches are intentional isolation for a non-blocking background title task; failures log or no-op instead of interrupting the user reply. The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, manually titled, or unreadable sessions.

Why does this matter now?

- Why it matters / User impact: Users with many saved sessions only had manual names, first-message fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, so session history was hard to scan and search. When `sessionTitle.enabled` is true, users can identify conversations by concise stored titles instead of first-message snippets or ids.

What is the intended outcome?

- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the scoped code update after focused validation, local real gateway proof, Control UI visual proof, and passing local ClawSweeper review; maintainer product/privacy/auth acceptance remains maintainer-owned before merge.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- What did NOT change: No unrelated behavior, no default enablement, no migration/backfill, no manual rename UI, no channel/provider/plugin capability change, no agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior change, and no ConfigIO or generic session-store merge policy change.
- Out of scope: Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.

What does success look like?

Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names and session activity ordering; gateway and Control UI rows can display and search the generated title.

What should reviewers focus on?

- Architecture / source-of-truth check: `autoTitle` is persisted as session metadata and projected outward; gateway and UI do not maintain a second title source. Runtime auth selection for this path is kept behind internal runtime code so the public runtime-auth helper contract is not expanded.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan: Related context is tracked in #89705. This update is scoped to the existing PR branch for #77165 and does not open a competing new PR or broaden the public provider-auth helper contract.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #77165

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #89705

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

ClawSweeper asked for explicit privacy/cost framing and Mantis-style visual proof that generated titles show up in the Control UI session list and search.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Enabled sessions can generate a durable `autoTitle`, expose it through `openclaw sessions --json` and gateway `sessions.list`, and render/search it in the Control UI session list.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw run with isolated state, synthetic prompts only, `sessionTitle.enabled: true`, a local mock OpenAI provider, and a real local gateway. Control UI proof used the real Control UI Vite bundle with a browser-injected mock gateway payload shaped like `sessions.list` rows containing `autoTitle` only.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran synthetic direct-user turns through the embedded agent session store, observed title generation through the production `maybeGenerateSessionTitle` path, queried `openclaw sessions --json`, queried gateway `sessions.list`, searched gateway sessions by the generated title, then loaded the Control UI session list with an `autoTitle`-only row and searched for that title.

External-model proof remains a disclosed limitation rather than a hidden code claim.

## Tests and validation

- Gateway session event test added after the ClawSweeper sandbox limitation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts` — passed 2 files / 48 tests.
- Local ClawSweeper commit review on the current committed diff: `result=nothing_found`, `confidence=high`, `highest_severity=none`, `check_conclusion=success`.

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Scenario locked in: Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names and session activity ordering.
- Coverage includes config opt-in, runtime model/auth forwarding, transcript filtering, input caps, manual title precedence, stale async write skip, post-reply metadata notification, activity timestamp preservation for generated-title writes, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway row/search/event behavior, and Control UI event patch/filter/display behavior.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The feature spans title creation, persistence, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway projection, and UI projection; the final diff removes earlier nonessential `sessions_list`, ConfigIO, generic store merge, test-routing, and public helper expansion work.

If no test was added, why not?

Tests were added and updated across title generation, auth-profile routing, gateway projection, CLI JSON output, session reset/rollover behavior, and Control UI rendering/search.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes, but only when `sessionTitle.enabled` is explicitly set to true. Default behavior remains unchanged.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. This adds a default-off `sessionTitle` config group and additive `autoTitle` session metadata. There is no migration/backfill.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. When explicitly enabled, the background title task can send bounded direct-user transcript excerpts to the selected title model using the session model/auth-profile routing.

What is the highest-risk area?

- Risk labels considered: compatibility, session-state, public config/schema, auth-provider routing, availability, privacy/cost boundary.
- Risk explanation: The highest-risk area is privacy/cost from sending transcript excerpts to the selected title model when the feature is explicitly enabled.

How is that risk mitigated?

- Why acceptable: The feature is opt-in/default-off; it sends only direct user text, skips heartbeat, internal-system, tool-mediated, media-only, or textless records, caps both per-message and total model input, skips manual-title sessions, guards stale writes by `sessionId`, writes `autoTitle` without refreshing `updatedAt`, runs after reply delivery, and logs/no-ops on title failures without changing the user reply.

target.title: improve(ui): flatten chat tool-call rows into a scannable list
target.body:
Closes #99760

## What Problem This Solves

Tool calls in the Control UI chat render as heavily decorated nested cards: the `Activity: N tools` group draws a bordered card, every tool message inside it draws another bubble box, and the summary button on top adds an accent gradient, an inset highlight, and a `0 8px 22px` drop shadow. Long tool summaries wrap across several lines. Dense agent sessions become hard to scan — a single 8-tool activity group fills an entire viewport.

Part of the box stacking is a CSS ordering bug: `components.css` begins with `@import "./chat.css"`, so its legacy `.chat-bubble` and `.chat-tool-card` blocks load after `chat/grouped.css`/`chat/tool-cards.css` and override the intended `.chat-bubble--tool-shell` resets (`padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent`). Each tool row therefore leaks a full bubble box underneath the summary pill.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool rows are now flat one-line rows (chevron + tool icon + label + mono detail, ellipsized), the activity group header is a flat clickable row, and its body is grouped by a thin left rule instead of a card. Expanded tool detail keeps soft tinted input/output blocks without card chrome; canvas/document previews keep their frame because they embed external content. Error states remain explicit (red icon/label plus `Error` badge, error groups still auto-expand). The duplicated legacy chat-bubble/tool-card CSS in `components.css` is deleted and the canonical `.chat-bubble` base in `chat/grouped.css` is reconciled to today's computed style, so normal user/assistant bubbles render unchanged. Dead render paths (`renderToolCardSidebar`, never-taken `renderToolDataBlock` branches) and their orphaned CSS are removed.

## User Impact

Chat sessions with tool activity are dramatically denser and calmer: an 8-tool activity group shrinks from roughly a full screen of stacked cards to a few compact rows, in both light and dark themes. Collapsed rows clamp to one line; the full command and output remain one click away. No behavior changes: expand/collapse, error badges, sidebar open, and previews all work as before.

## Evidence

Before/after with the same seeded conversation (mock gateway fixture, light and dark, collapsed/expanded/detail states):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Light, activity expanded | ![before light](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/a418aca1ccac81ee1123692463ebd70b/raw/before-light.png) | ![after light](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/a418aca1ccac81ee1123692463ebd70b/raw/after-light.png) |

| Light, tool detail expanded | ![before detail](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/a418aca1ccac81ee1123692463ebd70b/raw/before-light-detail.png) | ![after detail](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/a418aca1ccac81ee1123692463ebd70b/raw/after-light-detail.png) |

target.title: fix: store usage-cost pricing fingerprint once
target.body:
Closes #99511

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with large session histories would get oversized `.usage-cost-cache.json` files because the same `pricingFingerprint` string was duplicated on every cached file entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage-cost cache now stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache-object level and bumps the cache format to version 5 so older version 4 caches rebuild cleanly. Freshness checks compare the cache-level fingerprint, and refresh clears old entries when the active pricing fingerprint changes so stale cost totals are not reused across pricing changes.

## User Impact

Large usage-cost caches are smaller and cheaper to parse/rewrite. Usage-cost totals and session summaries keep the same behavior, while older v4 cache files rebuild automatically on the next refresh.

## Evidence

People downloading OpenClaw for Mac could not complete setup from the app alone when the CLI, Node.js, and Gateway were not already installed. Fresh local installs also exposed redundant pairing approvals for the app's own Mac node.

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach the current-generation Hunyuan `hy3` model or the TokenPlan endpoint. Adds a second provider id `tencent-tokenplan` alongside the existing `tencent-tokenhub`, expands the catalog, and wires auth / onboarding / reasoning-effort end-to-end so both endpoints are first-class:

target.title: fix(markdown-core): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in parseFrontmatterBlock
target.body:
## Summary
Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of the `in` operator in `parseFrontmatterBlock()` to prevent prototype chain pollution when merging line-parsed frontmatter entries.

## What Problem This Solves
When YAML frontmatter contains a key named after an `Object.prototype` property (e.g., `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`) with a `null` value, the key is **silently dropped** from the output.

**Root cause**: `coerceYamlFrontmatterValue(null)` returns `undefined`, causing the YAML parser to skip the key. The inline line parser still captures it, but the merge step at `frontmatter.ts:225` uses `key in merged` — which traverses the prototype chain. Since `"toString" in {}` is `true` (it finds `Object.prototype.toString`), the inline value is also discarded, and the user's data is lost.

**Code evidence**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts:225`, the code checks `if (!(key in merged))` — but `merged = {}` inherits from `Object.prototype`, so prototype keys are falsely detected as "already present".

## Root Cause
- The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, not just own properties
- `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022+) correctly checks only the object's own properties
- `Object.hasOwn` is already used 15+ times across the codebase (`src/infra/`, `src/param-key.ts`, `packages/agent-core/`, etc.) — this was the one remaining `in` operator usage on a plain object

## Why This Fix
- **Minimal**: 1-line change, no behavioral impact on normal keys
- **Consistent**: matches existing `Object.hasOwn` usage pattern in the codebase
- **Correct**: `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` is the semantically correct check for "does this object own this property"
- **Regression-safe**: normal keys pass unchanged; only prototype keys are affected

## Evidence
- **Before**: `toString: null` in YAML frontmatter → output `{title: "Hello"}` (toString **lost**)
- **After**: `toString: null` in YAML frontmatter → output `{title: "Hello", toString: "null"}` (toString **preserved**)
- All 4 prototype keys tested: toString, constructor, valueOf, hasOwnProperty — all preserved
- Normal keys regression check: passed

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-frontmatter.mjs
FAIL: 'toString' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'toString' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
FAIL: 'constructor' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'constructor' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
FAIL: 'valueOf' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'valueOf' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
FAIL: 'hasOwnProperty' is an own property of the result
FAIL: 'hasOwnProperty' value equals "null" (got: undefined)
PASS: normal key 'title' preserved (got: "Hello")

8 FAILED
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-frontmatter.mjs
PASS: 'toString' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'toString' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: 'constructor' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'constructor' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: 'valueOf' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'valueOf' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: 'hasOwnProperty' is an own property of the result
PASS: 'hasOwnProperty' value equals "null" (got: "null")
PASS: normal key 'title' preserved (got: "Hello")

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check`: passed (only pre-existing `npm shrinkwrap guard` failure, unrelated)
- Manual verification: 4 prototype keys + normal keys regression tested
- Diff: 1 line changed, 1 file

target.title: fix(reply): suppress post-tool-send meta commentary as duplicate reply
target.body:
Closes #96681

## What Problem This Solves

After an agent calls the `message` tool (`action=send`) to deliver its main reply in a turn, models often append a short trailing meta-acknowledgement to their final reply — patterns like `已发 #22141`, `Sent above`, `核心回答如下`, `OK`, `Roger`, `Got it`, `主回复已发 (#xxx)`, `已发, 不再追加总结`, `Sent. Replied in thread.`, `Done.`, `Okay`, `OK, that's the fix.`

These acks carry no information beyond the message-tool send that already went out, but OpenClaw currently delivers them as a **second** visible message in the channel — a well-known duplicate-reply failure mode (F30 / F31).

The existing `filterMessagingToolDuplicates` only catches full-content duplicates via substring match with a 10-char minimum, so short meta-acks (e.g. `已发 #22141`, 9 chars) escape the floor and reach the channel as a second visible message. The current dedupe is correct for "is this a rephrasing of something I already sent" but does not handle "is this an agent ack of its own tool call".

## Fix

This patch adds a complementary filter — `filterMessagingToolMetaCommentary` — that recognises post-tool-send meta commentary by pattern (Chinese + English) and suppresses it from the final reply payload. Wired into both `agent-runner-payloads.ts` and `followup-delivery.ts` **after** the existing content-dedupe filter, so the two compose without changing each other's behaviour.

The new filter is intentionally conservative:

- **Only fires when a message-tool send has already happened this turn** (`sentTexts.length > 0`). Agents with no message-tool sends are unaffected and short acks still pass through normally.
- **Length-capped at 200 chars** and only matches anchored ack patterns.
- **Substantial trailing content after the ack (> 20 chars) is treated as a real reply** — e.g. `已发. Now let me explain the architecture ...` is **NOT** suppressed.
- **Media payloads are always preserved**, even if the caption is meta-ack.

### Patterns matched

| Group | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Chinese standalone acks | `已发`, `已发送`, `已发 #22141`, `已发, 不再追加`, `主回复已发`, `主回复已发 (#xxx)`, `核心回答如下`, `总结如下`, `已发完成` |
| English standalone acks | `Sent`, `Sent above`, `Sent #22141`, `Sent.`, `Sent. Replied in thread.`, `Done.`, `Done`, `OK.`, `OK, that's the fix.`, `Roger`, `Roger that.`, `Got it`, `Got it.`, `Okay`, `Gotcha` |
| Suppressed prefix acks | `Replied`, `Replied above`, `Replied in thread`, `See above`, `As above` |
| CJK with optional trailing ref | `已发 #N`, `已发送 (#N)`, `主回复已发 (#N)` |

### Why a second filter, not extending the first

The existing content dedupe is correct for its purpose (substring match against `sentTexts`, 10-char floor). Extending it to 0-char would break legitimate short replies. A separate axis — "is this an ack of my own tool call" — only fires when there is a `message` tool send in the same turn, and only against a pattern list. The two filters compose: an ack that also matches the sent text still gets caught by the content filter; an ack that doesn't (e.g. `OK`, `Sent above` after a long body) gets caught by the new one.

## Evidence

### Test coverage (added in `reply-payloads.test.ts`)

New test cases for `filterMessagingToolMetaCommentary`:
- Suppresses `已发`, `已发 #22141`, `已发, 不再追加总结` after a `message` send
- Suppresses `Sent above`, `Sent.`, `Sent #22141`, `OK.`, `Roger`, `Got it`, `Done.` after a `message` send
- **Preserves** `OK.` when there is no prior message-tool send (ack is the entire reply)
- **Preserves** `已发. Now let me explain the architecture ...` (substantial trailing content)
- **Preserves** `Roger the new release looks good` (pattern doesn't anchor)
- **Preserves** media payloads (any caption containing a meta-ack is kept if the payload has media)
- Composition: ack after a long body that does not match sent text — only the meta filter catches it
- Composition: ack that also matches a substring of sent text — content filter catches it first, meta filter has nothing to do

### CI status on this PR (run 28152284825)

- ✅ `check-lint`
- ✅ `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`
- ✅ `check-shrinkwrap`, `check-dependencies`, `check-guards`
- ✅ `check-session-accessor-boundary`, `check-session-transcript-reader-boundary`
- ✅ `check-additional-boundaries-a/bcd`, `check-additional-extension-{channels,bundled,package-boundary}`
- ✅ `check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture`
- ✅ `checks-fast-bundled-protocol`, `checks-fast-bun-launcher`
- ✅ `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-a/b`, `checks-fast-contracts-channels-a/b`
- ✅ `checks-node-compact-small-{1..10,whole-1,2,3}`, `checks-node-compact-large-{1,2,3,whole-1}`
- ✅ `build-artifacts`, `QA Smoke CI`, `preflight`, `security-fast`
- ✅ CodeQL `Security High` (core-auth-secrets, channel-runtime-boundary, network-ssrf-boundary, mcp-process-tool-boundary, plugin-trust-boundary, actions)
- ✅ OpenGrep (precise diff scan + OSS)
- ✅ Dependency Guard, Security Sensitive Guard, Workflow Sanity
- ✅ ClawSweeper Dispatch, Labeler
- ✅ `auto-response` (ClawSweeper)
- ❌ `Real behavior proof` — see "PR body format check" below

### PR body format check failure

The `Real behavior proof` check (`scripts/github/real-behavior-proof-check.mjs`) is a **PR body format gate** for external contributors, not a behavioral test. On this PR it failed with:

> External PRs must include authored What Problem This Solves and Evidence sections.

The original PR body had `## Problem` and `## Fix` headings. This updated body renames/expands those into the required `## What Problem This Solves` and `## Evidence` sections above. No code change. Re-running the check is expected to flip to green.

### Files changed (8 files, +225 / −3)

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-payloads-dedupe.ts` — add `filterMessagingToolMetaCommentary` + pattern tables
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-payloads-dedupe.runtime.ts` — runtime helpers (trim, length cap, anchor matcher)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-payloads.ts` — wire new filter into the dedupe pipeline
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts` — call the new filter after the existing content-dedupe
- `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.ts` — same wiring for the followup path
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/messaging-dedupe.ts` — re-export the new filter for shared use
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.ts` — surface the filter in the embedded helper API
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-payloads.test.ts` — test cases listed above

### Live behavior

Local repro of the original issue, after applying this patch, on a Telegram-routed reply that includes a trailing `已发 #22141`:
- Before: 2 visible messages (main reply + `已发 #22141`)
- After: 1 visible message (main reply only; ack suppressed)

Same result on Discord and Signal (both go through `deliverOutboundPayloads`).
